rule.title: WMI Persistence
rule.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin oscd.community

es.summary: Se registró en el log WMI-Activity un enlace filtro-consumidor con un consumidor de script o de línea de comandos (5861), o un filtro de eventos permanente (5859). Puede indicar persistencia mediante suscripciones WMI.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos 5861 de Microsoft-Windows-WMI-Activity/Operational que mencionan ActiveScriptEventConsumer, CommandLineEventConsumer o CommandLineTemplate, y cualquier evento 5859. Excluye el filtro SCM Event Provider del grupo Administradores (S-1-5-32-544), que es legítimo.
es.why_it_matters: Una suscripción WMI permanente (ATT&CK T1546.003) ejecuta un comando o script, a menudo como SYSTEM, cuando ocurre un evento, por ejemplo al arrancar o cada cierto tiempo. Sobrevive a reinicios y no aparece en las claves Run ni en las tareas programadas.
triage_steps: Lea el texto del evento 5861: anote el nombre del Eventfilter, el Consumer y el valor de CommandLineTemplate o ScriptText. Busque PowerShell codificado, rutas en Users\Public o Temp, o URLs.
En el 5859 revise Query, Provider, NamespaceName, User y PossibleCause. Una consulta sobre Win32_PerfFormattedData o __InstanceModificationEvent con WITHIN suele indicar un disparador temporizado.
Enumere en vivo con Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\subscription las clases __EventFilter, __EventConsumer y __FilterToConsumerBinding, y confirme que la suscripción sigue presente.
Identifique el proceso creador: revise los eventos 5857/5860 del mismo host y, si existen, Sysmon 19/20/21 y Security 4688 en +/- 15 minutos.
Determine qué usuario o cuenta creó la suscripción y si tiene logons recientes inusuales (4624) o movimiento lateral desde otra IP.
Busque el mismo nombre de filtro o consumidor en otros endpoints, y revise alertas anteriores del host y del usuario.
false_positives: Agentes de gestión o monitoreo de hardware (por ejemplo drivers de salud de HP o Dell) que registran consumidores permanentes.
Software de inventario, backup o EDR que usa suscripciones WMI para vigilar servicios o el hardware.
Scripts de administradores o GPO que crean suscripciones WMI documentadas.
response_steps: Verifique con el dueño del sistema o con el inventario de software si la suscripción es conocida antes de actuar.
Si es maliciosa, aísle el endpoint y exporte el filtro, el consumidor y el binding, junto con el binario o script referenciado, como evidencia.
Elimine el binding, el consumidor y el filtro con Remove-CimInstance solo después de documentarlos; elimine el payload asociado.
Revise y rote las credenciales de la cuenta creadora y busque la misma suscripción en toda la flota.
Si se confirman consumidores legítimos, documéntelos y agregue una exclusión específica por nombre y ruta.
es.severity_rationale: Medium es adecuado: la persistencia WMI es una técnica de alto impacto, pero algunos agentes legítimos generan estos eventos y la regla tiene pocas pruebas en entornos reales.

en.summary: The WMI-Activity log recorded a filter-to-consumer binding with a script or command-line consumer (5861), or a permanent event filter (5859). This may mean someone set up persistence through a WMI subscription.
en.what_it_detects: Event 5861 in Microsoft-Windows-WMI-Activity/Operational that mentions ActiveScriptEventConsumer, CommandLineEventConsumer or CommandLineTemplate, plus any event 5859. The legitimate SCM Event Provider filter owned by Administrators (S-1-5-32-544) is excluded.
en.why_it_matters: A permanent WMI event subscription (ATT&CK T1546.003) runs a command or script, often as SYSTEM, when a trigger fires, such as at startup or on a timer. It survives reboots and stays out of Run keys and scheduled tasks.
triage_steps: Read the 5861 event text. Note the Eventfilter name, the Consumer and the CommandLineTemplate or ScriptText value. Look for encoded PowerShell, Users\Public or Temp paths, or URLs.
For 5859, review Query, Provider, NamespaceName, User and PossibleCause. A query on Win32_PerfFormattedData or __InstanceModificationEvent with WITHIN usually means a timed trigger.
Enumerate root\subscription live with Get-CimInstance: __EventFilter, __EventConsumer and __FilterToConsumerBinding. Confirm the subscription is still present.
Find the creating process. Check 5857/5860 on the same host and, if available, Sysmon 19/20/21 and Security 4688 within +/- 15 minutes.
Identify the account that created the subscription. Check it for unusual recent logons (4624) or lateral movement from another IP.
Hunt for the same filter or consumer name on other endpoints. Review earlier alerts for this host and user.
false_positives: Hardware management or monitoring agents, such as HP or Dell health drivers, that register permanent consumers.
Inventory, backup or EDR software that uses WMI subscriptions to watch services or hardware.
Documented admin scripts or GPOs that create WMI subscriptions.
response_steps: Before acting, check with the system owner or the software inventory whether the subscription is known.
If it is malicious, isolate the endpoint. Export the filter, consumer and binding, plus the binary or script they reference, as evidence.
Document the binding, consumer and filter, then remove them with Remove-CimInstance and delete the related payload.
Review and rotate the creating account's credentials. Hunt for the same subscription across the fleet.
If the consumers are legitimate, document them and add a narrow exclusion by name and path.
en.severity_rationale: Medium fits because WMI persistence has high impact, but some legitimate agents produce these events and the rule has had little real-world testing.

positive.description: Event 5861 binding a filter to a CommandLineEventConsumer that starts a binary from Users\Public

event.message: Namespace = //./root/subscription; Eventfilter = SysUpdater (refer to its activate eventid:5859); Consumer = CommandLineEventConsumer="SysUpdater"; PossibleCause = Binding EventFilter: instance of __EventFilter { EventNamespace = "root\\cimv2"; Name = "SysUpdater"; Query = "SELECT * FROM __InstanceModificationEvent WITHIN 60 WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System'"; QueryLanguage = "WQL"; }; Perm. Consumer: instance of CommandLineEventConsumer { CommandLineTemplate = "C:\\Users\\Public\\updater.exe"; Name = "SysUpdater"; };

positive.description: Event 5859 for a permanent filter registered by a non-SCM provider

event.Query: SELECT * FROM __InstanceModificationEvent WITHIN 60 WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfOS_System'

negative.description: Legitimate 5859 for the SCM Event Provider owned by Administrators, removed by the filter
Event 5861 binding to an NTEventLogEventConsumer, with none of the script or command-line consumer keywords

event.message: Namespace = //./root/subscription; Eventfilter = HWHealthFilter (refer to its activate eventid:5859); Consumer = NTEventLogEventConsumer="HWHealthLogger"; PossibleCause = Binding EventFilter: instance of __EventFilter { Name = "HWHealthFilter"; QueryLanguage = "WQL"; }; Perm. Consumer: instance of NTEventLogEventConsumer { Name = "HWHealthLogger"; SourceName = "HWHealth"; };
